
If there is a JavaScript code fragment
 window.i=0;
 window.k=0;
 window.j=0;
 function callframe(){
    console.log( 'i=', i++ );
    window.requestAnimationFrame( callframe );
 };
 console.log( 'k=', k++ );

 //end of fragment

and if there is a user click event attached to html button

 <button onclick="console.log('j=', j++);">click</button>

then can code thread i++ and code thread j++; run concurrently or JavaScript will always make them wait for each other?

///GPT answer:
In a normal browser page, i++ and j++ do not execute concurrently on the same JavaScript thread.

JavaScript in the page runs on a single main thread/event loop. Your two pieces of code are scheduled as separate tasks/callbacks, but when one callback is executing, the other waits.
